featuredStory.title: William E Lane of Boston
featuredStory.subtitle: Exhibit 1 · Opening exhibit
featuredStory.summary: William E Lane of Boston (cordwainer) anchors the opening exhibit: Hartford and Lynn appearances, freeman 1657, and the Mary Brewer marriage — chronology that later Lanes extend from.
historianNotes: Book narrative cites Hist. Gen. Reg. XII, 196 for harmonizing Hartford (Samuel b. 8 Aug. 1648) and Lynn (1651); verify against NEHGR and town records.
First church Boston, Mary’s death 1656, second marriage to Mary Brewer (Roxbury) — use as baseline before Stratham and later migrations.

citations.label: NEHGR — New England Historical and Genealogical Register (vol. 12 context; see XII:196 in book)

prominentLanes.caption: Opening exhibit · colonial New England chronology anchor (same as featured panel)
prominentLanes.blurb: Some records may be harmonized if William E Lane were residing in Hartford, Connecticut, where he had a son, Samuel, born 8 August 1648, and visiting in Lynn in 1651 [see Hist. Gen. Reg. XII, 196]. He was made freeman 6 May 1657. His wife Mary, a member of the first church in Boston (probably from England), died 22 May 1656; and he married (2) 21 August 1656, by Richard Bellingham, Deputy Governor, to Mary (daughter of Thomas) Brewer of Roxbury, Massachusetts. Her father, Goodman Brewer, in 1642 resided in Ipswich, removed afterward to Roxbury, and died at the home of his son-in-law, Thomas Webster, in Hampton, 3 March 1689–90.

prominentLanes.caption: Second wife of William I · married 21 Aug. 1656 (Boston)
prominentLanes.blurb: Vol. I: daughter of Thomas Brewer of Roxbury; married William Lane after the death of Mary (Kelway). Goodman Brewer later died at the home of his son-in-law Thomas Webster in Hampton (1689–90)—the Brewer and Webster lines thread through later Hampton and Chester narratives.
prominentLanes.imageCaption: Mary (Brewer) Lane — second household of William I (compilation portrait).

prominentLanes.caption: Stratham town clerk from 1774; Revolutionary-era NH diarist context
prominentLanes.blurb: Farmer, surveyor, deacon — his manuscript diary (1775–76) is a classic New Hampshire Revolutionary source.

prominentLanes.caption: Second generation · colonial Boston cordwainer; King Philip's War narrative (1675)
prominentLanes.blurb: Lane Genealogies (Vol. 1, 1891) states that in March 1675, age 22, he was a soldier in King Philip's War under Capt. Poole — not claiming muster-roll verification beyond the genealogy text.

prominentLanes.caption: Second generation · Boston; Turner company in same war (1676 narrative)
prominentLanes.blurb: Same compilation puts him under Capt. Turner in 1676 and explicitly ties him to the same company lineage where brother John Lane served under Capt. Poole in March 1675 — separate captain and year from John; not collapsed into "both under Poole."
prominentLanes.imageCaption: Samuel² Lane — Boston register line; Hadley and Turner company context in Vol. I.

prominentLanes.caption: Second-generation tailor; Boston · removal to Hampton 1686; Sarah Webster marriage
prominentLanes.blurb: Lane Genealogies (Vol. 1, 1891) summarizes Boston tailoring, joining North Church 1681, grant and removal to Hampton 1686, and wife Sarah (Thomas Webster line). The compilation also cites Tythinge Man Boston (May 5, 1686, spelling as printed) and Hampton parish assessment extracts via NEHGR IX:159; those are bookkeeping and civic context—not military proof. Daniel Webster ties in the book are treated here as compilation claims unless separately verified.

links.label: NEHGR — vol. 9 register context (book cites IX:159)

prominentLanes.displayName: Sarah Dickinson — Hadley; wife of Samuel² (Vol. 1)
prominentLanes.caption: Samuel² (Hadley) household; later captivity narrative in compilation
prominentLanes.blurb: Vol. 1 places Samuel² in Hadley with Sarah (Dickinson) and names their children’s births and marriages there or nearby (e.g. Suffield). The same tradition line includes her later hardship: widowhood, remarriage to Martin Kellogg, and the 1704 French and Indian raid taking her and children captive—reported in the compilation as family narrative, not as muster or court file.
prominentLanes.imageCaption: Sarah Dickinson Lane — Hadley household line; remarriage and 1704 captivity narrative in Vol. I.

prominentLanes.caption: m. John³ son of William²; Anthony Libbey / Black Point prose in book
prominentLanes.blurb: Vol. 1 (NEHGR IX:159 bundle): daughter of Anthony and Sarah Drake Libbey of Rye; married John Lane³ b. Boston 17 Feb. 1685. The same footnote block threads Libbey origins, 1690 Black Point incident, Portsmouth, Hampton church 1717, and Mary’s will legacy—genealogy-compilation tier only; not a substitute for town or court records.

prominentLanes.personQuery: John Lane Hampton 1709 Cornet Chester Hannah Lamprey
prominentLanes.caption: Father-generation anchor for Lt. Bennington line · mounted militia 1754
prominentLanes.blurb: Vol. 1 traces Hampton-born John⁴ to Chester with Hannah Lamprey and later Mary Knowles, farming and tavern-keeping—the compilation’s officer note for Sept. 1754 Cornet in a troop of horse is genealogy tier (check provincial rolls separately). Revolutionary officer sons Ezekiel and John Lt. descend from this cluster.
prominentLanes.imageCaption: Cornet John Lane — Chester horse troop, French and Indian frontier context.

prominentLanes.caption: Stickney regiment / Dearborn company (Vol. 1 compilation)
prominentLanes.blurb: Lane Genealogies (Vol. 1) assigns him lieutenant commission in Dearborn company, Stickney regiment, battlefield death Battle of Bennington Aug. 16, 1777—genealogy abstraction; corroborate with pension files and Compiled Military Service Records.

prominentLanes.displayName: Lt. John Lane — Bennington survivor, promoted
prominentLanes.personQuery: John Lane Chester Dearborn Stickney Bennington
prominentLanes.caption: Brother-branch officer line in same regiment cluster (Vol. 1)
prominentLanes.blurb: Vol. 1: second lieutenant July 1777 in Dearborn’s company, marched from Chester, present at Bennington Aug. 16, 1777; promoted after Ezekiel Lane fell—the book pairs the brothers deliberately; treat enlistment dates as pedigree until NH rolls confirm. Wife in the compilation is Mary (dau. of Benaiah and Mary Webster) of Chester (OCR “Coley“ garbage removed on the tree). A later descendant in the same Chester column bears the given name Webster Lane—a Vol. 1 naming echo of the Webster line only, not independent proof.

prominentLanes.displayName: John Lane — Bunker Hill to West Point (Chester enlistments)
prominentLanes.personQuery: John Lane Chester Hutchins Bunker Hill Poor regiment
prominentLanes.caption: Youth enlistment continuum in Vol. 1 Chester column
prominentLanes.blurb: Genealogy book strings Hutchins company / Bunker-or-Breed’s Hill involvement, Poor’s regiment enlistment March 1777, and Bartlett regiment duty at West Point in 1780—OCR quirks cleaned on the tree node but evidence tier remains familial abstraction.

prominentLanes.displayName: Daniel Lane — burying-ground donor; Gale regiment detail
prominentLanes.personQuery: Daniel Lane Gale regiment Chester burying ground
prominentLanes.caption: 26-day NJ deployment line (Aug. 1778) + civic contribution
prominentLanes.blurb: Vol. 1 combines benevolent-town fabric (family burying lot with cousin fencing circle) with a Revolutionary note: enlistment Aug. 5, 1778 in Col. Gale’s regiment destined for New Jersey for twenty-six days—confirm against pay lists before asserting campaign presence.

prominentLanes.caption: Parish and civic duty (William² branch, Vol. 1)
prominentLanes.blurb: Lane Genealogies Vol. 1 carries Thomas³ as a Hampton resident and sexton of the church who died 30 Aug. 1775, ae. 74—local church-care context only; no battlefield claim.

prominentLanes.caption: Compiled family anecdote only (Vol. 1)
prominentLanes.blurb: Vol. 1 states that Captain Matthias Lane in the War of 1812 declined the office of colonel—compilation anecdote until pay rolls or state papers corroborate; not a statement that he fought at a named action.

prominentLanes.caption: Popular Science Monthly (May 1884) profile—“Was He an Idiot?”—on a Hampton Falls man with calendrical gifts, described in period terms that overlap today’s “idiot savant” idea.
prominentLanes.blurb: Brother Levi E. Lane’s note in the Lane genealogy; national magazine piece on calendrical prodigy and singular abilities (illustrated read-along on-site).

prominentLanes.caption: Astrophysicist · Lane–Emden equation; lunar crater Lane; uncle of William Homer Lane in this tree
prominentLanes.blurb: Vol. I lists him under Mark Lane as first child: Exeter Academy, Yale 1846, coast survey in Washington. Standard biography adds Patent Office and Weights and Measures work and the gaseous-sun analysis behind stellar-structure theory. In this graph he is paternal uncle of William Homer Lane (id 108) and grand-uncle of Alderman Homer R Lane (id 112).
prominentLanes.imageCaption: Jonathan Homer Lane — astrophysicist; namesake of lunar crater Lane.

links.label: Lane Genealogies Vol. I — Internet Archive (context)

prominentLanes.caption: Mojave pioneer; established Lane's Crossing ranch and traveler store (1859)
prominentLanes.blurb: Veteran of the Mexican-American War and a Forty-niner, Captain Aaron G. Lane is presented here as a Victor Valley pioneer and the first permanent settler on the High Desert near the lower narrows of the Mojave River. In 1859 he established the ranch and traveler store at Lane's Crossing on the Mormon Road; the site later became a focal point for frontier conflict, law-enforcement pursuits, and Civil War-era instability in the San Bernardino corridor. Family note: Aaron G. Lane is Homer Lane's first cousin, three times removed.
prominentLanes.imageCaption: Captain Aaron G. Lane, Mojave River pioneer and founder of Lane's Crossing.

lunarExhibit.title: Lane crater observatory
lunarExhibit.subtitle: LROC QuickMap · USGS planetary names · “Lunar-5” spotlight
lunarExhibit.body: Jonathan Homer Lane’s solar models helped launch stellar structure theory. The Moon’s Lane crater (~54 km) sits in Mare Cognitum — explore it in NASA’s LROC QuickMap or read the official USGS feature sheet.

timelineEvents.title: Chronology Start
timelineEvents.description: William E Lane of Boston (cordwainer) is used as the opening narrative anchor.

timelineEvents.title: John Lane — Capt. Poole (Vol. 1 narrative)
timelineEvents.description: Lane Genealogies (Vol. 1): Mar. 1675, age 22, soldier under Capt. Poole in Philip’s/King Philip’s War—compilation wording; verify with muster sources separately.

timelineEvents.title: Samuel Lane — Turner; footnote Joshua — Wadsworth (Vol. 1)
timelineEvents.description: Vol. 1: Samuel² under Capt. Turner in the same-war company lineage tied to John’s 1675 Poole roll. Separate footnote (NEHGR IX:159 cluster) mentions a Joshua Lane in July 1676 under Capt. Wadsworth—do not collapse into Samuel or John without proof.

timelineEvents.title: William² & Sarah Webster (Vol. 1)
timelineEvents.description: Book: marriage 21 June 1680—Sarah (dau. of Thomas Webster) per Vol. 1; Daniel Webster pedigree claims flagged as compilation-only on-site.

timelineEvents.title: Hampton grant & Boston Tythinge Man (Vol. 1)
timelineEvents.description: Vol. 1: William² to Hampton on a grant of ten acres; Boston town meeting 5 May 1686—chosen Tythinge Man (printed spelling Tythinge).

timelineEvents.title: John³ (William²) & Mary Libbey — Rye marriage (Vol. 1)
timelineEvents.description: Book line: Boston-born John³ m. 7 Mar. 1709 Mary (Libbey) of Rye; Libbey-Black Point-Hampton prose sits in same reference cluster—compilation narrative tier.

timelineEvents.title: Captivity narrative — Sarah widow of Samuel (book text)
timelineEvents.description: OCR/book block: Kellogg marriage, Deerfield-era captivity strand—use as genealogical narrative only until matched to primary lists.

timelineEvents.title: Hampton assessments cited — NEHGR IX:159 (Vol. 1)
timelineEvents.description: Book excerpts Old Parish Hampton Dec. 1731 / Jan. 1732 lists (William, Joshua, Thomas holdings)—tax context, not service records.

timelineEvents.title: Chester Lane roster — Breed's/Bunker Hill youth enlistment strand (Vol. 1)
timelineEvents.description: John Lane (later Poor/Bartlett service in book lines) cites Capt. Hutchins company at seventeen during the June 1775 Charlestown fight—compilation pedigree; reconcile with Compiled Military Service Records.

timelineEvents.title: Thomas³ Lane — Hampton church sexton (Vol. 1)
timelineEvents.description: Vol. 1: William²’s son Thomas resided in Hampton as sexton of the parish church and died 30 Aug. 1775, ae. 74—parish civic life only; not a military-roll claim.

timelineEvents.title: Simon Lane — Elkins / Poor company; march Hampton → Medford (Vol. 1 p. 21)
timelineEvents.description: Genealogical abstraction only: III. Simon Lane (Thomas², William¹)—Capt. H. Elkins’s company, Col. E. Poor’s regiment in May 1775; the compilation states he marched 1 Aug. 1775 from Hampton to join the army at Medford, Mass. Not a roll-confirmed battle claim beyond Lane Genealogies Vol. 1 (1891), p. 21.

timelineEvents.title: 16 Aug. 1777 — Battle of Bennington (Lt. Ezekiel KIA; Lt. John promoted; Vol. 1)
timelineEvents.description: Book cluster: Lt. John Lane commissioned July 1777 Dearborn company, Stickney regiment, march from Chester, present at Bennington Aug. 16; Lt. Ezekiel Lane (same regiment context) killed that day—compilation pairing only until NH muster/service files confirm.

timelineEvents.title: Daniel Lane — Gale regiment NJ stint (Vol. 1)
timelineEvents.description: Aug. 5, 1778 enlistment narrative in Col. Gale’s regiment headed to New Jersey for twenty-six recorded days—civilian civic notes (burying-ground gift) anchored in same family cluster.

timelineEvents.title: Matthias Lane — War of 1812 anecdote (compilation only)
timelineEvents.description: Vol. 1: Captain Matthias Lane is said (in compilation) to have declined the office of colonel during the War of 1812—family anecdote until service records corroborate; does not assign him to any named battlefield.

timelineEvents.title: John Lane — Bartlett regiment at West Point (Vol. 1 Chester column)
timelineEvents.description: Book lists July-Oct. 1780 service with Col. T. Bartlett’s regiment guarding West Point after earlier Continental enlistments—treat chronology text as pedigree until corroborated.

timelineEvents.title: American History Context
timelineEvents.description: Colonial tensions shape New England family life and migration patterns.

timelineEvents.title: Jonathan Homer Lane
timelineEvents.description: Astrophysicist dies; later, lunar crater Lane is named for him (IAU).

historiansTeaser.title: Honoring the compilers
historiansTeaser.lede: Volume I (1891) was generations in the making. This site brings the original Lane genealogy book to life as an interactive family map, then adds newer family branches from our own research so descendants can reconnect with long-lost people, places, stories, and treasures.
